title: [Chapitre] IX et IX bis. [Ateliers] : notes manuscrites (05-15/07/1986).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting: the 'set-theoretic presentation' of the 'ateliers' (the 1986 lattice/Boolean-algebra formalism), where a correspondence between sets E and E' is given by its graph Γ ⊂ E×E'. Write f: Γ→E and f': Γ→E' for the two projections, giving the span E ←f− Γ −f'→ E'. Grothendieck observes that the correspondence factors as Γ = f'∘ᵗf: first the transpose ('inverse') of the map f, then the map f'. On power sets this is the composite P(E) → P(Γ) → P(E'), A ↦ f^{-1}(A) ↦ f'(f^{-1}(A)), i.e. α_*(A) = f'(f^{-1}(A)), which is made explicit on the next page.

He then characterizes the two kinds of factors by how they interact with complementation C.
- A correspondence of the form ᵗf (a 'comorphism') is exactly one whose induced map on power sets commutes with C. Proof: if R ⊂ X×Y has R_*(∁A) = ∁R_*(A), then R_*(X) = Y, so every y is related to some x. Also R_*({x1}) ∩ R_*(∁{x1}) = ∅, so no y is related to two distinct x. Hence R is the transpose of a map Y→X.
- Dually, a correspondence of the form f' (a 'morphism') is characterized by its transpose ᵗf' commuting with C. Indeed (ᵗf')_* = f'^{-1}.

An insertion, only partly legible, says the comorphisms can be characterized 'algebraically', in terms of correspondences of the general (lattice-theoretic) kind.

He closes by asking whether a similar decomposition holds in the general case of 'cartes disjonctives', or equivalently 'cartes spatiales'. These are the generalized correspondences between the lattices/'ateliers' Σ, Σ' (Conv(Σ,Σ')) studied on the surrounding pages, where the previous page noted that the lack of 'points' (atoms) obstructs defining C or ≤ on Conv(Σ,Σ'). The next page says these questions are not of direct consequence for the formalism and turns to characterizations of α_* via commutation with ∩ and relative complements, including injectivity of f'.

In modern terms: every relation is a tabulated span (map ∘ converse of map). Converses of maps are exactly the relations whose direct-image operator is a Boolean homomorphism. The open question is whether tabulations exist for 'relations' between point-free Boolean/lattice objects.
errors: No mathematical errors. The claim that comorphisms are exactly the correspondences whose direct image commutes with complementation is correct (it implicitly forces totality and single-valuedness), and dually for morphisms.
Notational looseness only: Γ denotes both the graph and the correspondence, and 'f'∘ᵗf' is composition of correspondences written right-to-left.

ideas.what: Every correspondence (relation) factors as the converse of a map followed by a map, through its graph: α_* = f'_* ∘ f^{-1}.
ideas.modern_name: Tabulation of relations / span representation (Rel as a quotient of Span(Set))
ideas.usually_credited_to: Folklore; formalized in allegory theory by Freyd–Scedrov (Categories, Allegories, 1990); spans going back to Bénabou
ideas.where_published: Correspondences via graphs are implicit throughout EGA/SGA; no specific locus known

ideas.what: Characterization of converses of maps ('comorphismes') as those correspondences whose power-set map commutes with complementation; maps ('morphismes') as those whose transpose does.
ideas.modern_name: Relations inducing Boolean homomorphisms of power sets are exactly converses of functions (discrete Stone/Jónsson–Tarski duality: complete atomic Boolean algebras ↔ sets)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Folklore; Jónsson–Tarski (Boolean algebras with operators, 1951) for operator–relation correspondence; Tarski/Lindenbaum for CABA–Set duality

ideas.what: Question: does an analogous factorization exist for general 'cartes disjonctives / cartes spatiales' between lattice-type objects ('ateliers') lacking points?
ideas.modern_name: Existence of tabulations in allegories of relations between locales / Boolean algebras (point-free relations)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Freyd–Scedrov (tabular allegories); Johnstone and Joyal–Tierney for relations in locale theory

missed.claim: Grothendieck poses, and leaves unanswered here, whether general point-free correspondences ('cartes disjonctives', equivalently 'cartes spatiales') between his 'ateliers' admit a factorization into a comorphism followed by a morphism, analogous to graph factorization for sets. This is essentially the tabularity question for an allegory of point-free relations. Freyd–Scedrov and locale theory treat it, but there is no indication Grothendieck pursued it, and he himself judges it of no direct consequence on the next page.
missed.quote: Y a-t-il une décomposition similaire dans le cas général des cartes disjonctives, ou ce qui revient au même, cartes spatiales ?
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Of mainly historical interest. It shows Grothendieck in 1986 independently arriving at the allegory/tabulation viewpoint for point-free spaces, in his unpublished 'ateliers' formalism. Mathematically the question is covered by existing theory of relations in regular categories and locales.

deep.surprise_reason: The content is the standard span factorization of a relation and an elementary characterization of converses of maps via complement-preservation. The only non-routine element is an open question that the later allegory and locale literature addresses, which Grothendieck himself sets aside.
transcription_corrections: '(entraînant[?] liens :' and 'donnant[?] liens :' are most likely '(donnant lieu :' in both places, i.e. 'giving rise to A ↦ f^{-1}(A), P(E)→P(Γ)' and 'B ↦ f'(B), P(Γ)→P(E')'.
The interlinear insertion reads more like '+algébriquement en termes des corr. de Sp...+' (possibly 'Spatiales' or 'Σ') than 'explicitement en termes de corr. de foncteurs'.
'caractériser [-par la propriété de commuter-] à C': the struck phrase seems to be partly retained ('par la propriété de commuter à C'), consistent with the parallel sentence for f'.
Last line: 'ou ce qui revient au[x] mêmes, cartes spatiales ?'; 'cartes disjonctives' looks right.
The handwritten page number at top is 100; '103' at bottom left is the archive foliation.
